text:
Dylan DeMelo had five points in four games through Thursday, per RotoWire, including two assists in the comeback win in Montreal that ended Winnipeg's nine-game skid. The Winnipeg Free Press picked a good week to profile him in its "Get to know your Jets" series.

Enjoy the points; they won't last at this rate. He has 8 in 17 games, a points rate of 1.39 per 60 minutes against a range of 0.6 to 1.1 we'd expect, and Winnipeg has scored 6.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His own offense is close to zero (0.71 expected goals).

What lasts is the rest. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 90th percentile last season at taking chances away, most of his value from even-strength defense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a surprise: he was in the 95th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists, so the passing is real even if the points are inflated. His skating isn't (6th percentile top speed). He's 33, a 2011 sixth-round pick, with 469 games as a Jet. His minutes are down two a game lately, worth watching as Winnipeg reshuffles. We project about 26 points.
headline: DeMelo's sudden offense
